Point maps, with clusters

Source: R/map.R
ptmap.Rd

ptmap() draws points on a map at an aspect of 1, optionally coloured by cluster: a result of dbscn() or a cluster number per point. Each cluster has its own colour and point shape (so the clusters read in grey print too) and its number at its centre, the mean of its points; noise is drawn as grey crosses. The box and the cluster centres are computed by the compiled kernel; R only draws. plot() of a dbscn() result draws it through ptmap(), given the points it was found in.

Usage

ptmap(x, y = NULL, cl = NULL, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'dbscn'
plot(x, y, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

Arguments

x

The points: a numeric matrix or data frame of two columns (x and y), or the x coordinates with y. For plot(), a result of dbscn().

y

NULL or the y coordinates, one per value of x. For plot(), the points the clusters were found in, as x of ptmap().

cl

NULL, a result of dbscn(), or the cluster of each point: a whole number from 1, NA for noise.

...

Passed to graphics::plot.window().

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

NULL (the palette) or colours, one per cluster.

pal

NULL (the session palette, see plotopt()) or a palette name for blpal().

Value

Invisibly, a list: pts, a data frame of the points (x, y, cl the cluster or NA, col and pch as drawn); cent, one row per cluster number from 1 to the largest (cl, the centre x and y, NaN for a number no point has, and n its points); and bbox, the box drawn (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax).

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- rbind(cbind(rnorm(30, 0, 0.2), rnorm(30, 0, 0.2)),
           cbind(rnorm(30, 3, 0.2), rnorm(30, 1, 0.2)),
           cbind(runif(10, -2, 5), runif(10, -2, 3)))
ptmap(p)

d <- dbscn(p, eps = 0.3, minpts = 5)
plot(d, p)
